the selected Zygomycetes can be used as a biotechnological tool for the production of single cell oil from olive mill wastewater, which is rich in phenolic compounds.
the olive mill wastewater as a sole carbon source in submerged culture can be used as substrate for single-cell oil production by some Zygomycete strains.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of single cell oil (SCO) by Zygomycete strains on olive mill wastewater (OWMW), a byproduct of the olive oil production industry, as sole carbon source.

the development of an innovative process for the conversion of OMW into lipids rich in PUFAs and the simultaneous removal of phenolic compounds by the use of selected strains of Zygorhynchaceae, a group of filamentous fungi which are known to be rich in lipids and to produce PUFAs.
the production of single cell oil by selected strains of zygomycetes, which could be used in the future as an alternative source for PUFA and other lipids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

OMW is an excellent substrate for PUFA biosynthesis and storage by Zygomycete microorganisms, which could be used for the production of high added value liposubstances, in parallel with a substantial phenolic removal from this waste stream.
OMW could be used as a substrate for the production of lipids by selected Zygomycetes strains, and in particular for T. elegans.
the OMW is an excellent substrate for the production of PUFA rich lipids by Z. moelleria and T. elegans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of Zygomycetous fungi for the production of high added value liposoluble products from OMW is a promising approach, which can contribute to a better OMW management and to the valorization of this by-product.
the selected Zygomycetes strains were able to grow on OMWs as sole carbon source and produce a significant amount of lipids, rich in PUFA.
Zygomycetes can be considered as promising candidates for the biotechnological conversion of OMW to high added value liposoluble compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OMW can be used as a sole carbon source for lipid biosynthesis by Zygomycete fungi, with high PUFA content.

the use of Zygomycete strains, in particular T. elegans, for the production of high added value PUFA-rich lipids from OMW, can be considered a viable and sustainable process for the management of this problematic waste.
